faculty: Computer Science and Engineering (Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering)
duration: 3 years Bachelor's (180 ECTS) + 2 years Master's (120 ECTS), integrated 3+2 track; graduates automatically continue into the Master's Programme in Computer Science and Engineering; 33 study places annually; non-EU fee reduced by a 30% tuition-fee waiver from the 2nd year of study; SAT test required for applicants without a Finnish matriculation/IB/EB/DIA-RP qualification

faculty: Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering
duration: 3 years Bachelor's (180 ECTS) + 2 years Master's (120 ECTS), integrated 3+2 track; page states graduates continue to a Master's in EITHER Electronics OR Wireless Communications Engineering (a genuine either/or choice, not one fixed continuation programme) - quote: "continue their education further to a master's in either Electronics or Wireless Communications Engineering"; non-EU fee reduced by a 30% tuition-fee waiver from the 2nd year of study

faculty: Software Engineering and Information Systems (Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering)
duration: 3 years Bachelor's (180 ECTS) + 2 years Master's (120 ECTS), integrated 3+2 track; graduates automatically continue into the Master's Programme in Software Engineering and Information Systems; non-EU fee reduced by a 30% tuition-fee waiver from the 2nd year of study

faculty: Computer Science and Engineering (Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering)
duration: 2 years, 120 ECTS; four combinable study options: Applied Computing, Artificial Intelligence, Computer Engineering, Cyber Security; based on research from four groups within the CSE unit (Biomimetics and Intelligent Systems Group, Center for Machine Vision and Signal Analysis, Center for Ubiquitous Computing, Centre for Atmospheric Research); non-EU fee reduced by a 30% tuition-fee waiver from the 2nd year of study

faculty: Advanced Electronics Centre (AEC) (Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering)
duration: 2 years, 120 ECTS; 60 study places; EUR-ACE accredited; three study tracks (Electronics Design; Electronics Materials and Components; Future Electronics and Measurement Techniques) taught by the Circuits and Systems (CAS), Microelectronics (MIC) and Opto-Electronics and Measurement Techniques (OPEM) research units - these three units together make up the Advanced Electronics Centre (AEC) per the faculty's own structure page, so AEC attribution is inferred from the named sub-units rather than an explicit "AEC administers this programme" statement; non-EU fee reduced by a 30% tuition-fee waiver from the 2nd year of study

faculty: Software Engineering and Information Systems (Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering)
duration: 2 years, 120 ECTS; two combinable tracks (Software Engineering; Information Systems); non-EU fee reduced by a 30% tuition-fee waiver from the 2nd year of study

faculty: Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering
duration: 2 years, 120 ECTS; a coordinated academic collaboration between University of Oulu and University of Vaasa ("not a joint degree") - students apply to one university and take cross-university courses, building a study path combining courses from both; no unit more specific than the Faculty stated on the programme's own page; non-EU fee reduced by a 30% tuition-fee waiver from the 2nd year of study

faculty: Centre for Wireless Communications (CWC) (Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering)
duration: 2 years, 120 ECTS; EUR-ACE accredited; run in tight collaboration with the 6G Flagship research programme; two study options (Radio Access and Networks / WCE-RAN; RF Engineering / WCE-RF), final track selection considers academic background and possibly an interview; CWC attribution is well-established (the programme's own materials are hosted on CWC's oulu.fi/cwc subdomain, and independent sources quote CWC as "in charge of the programme") but a direct fetch of the CWC-hosted page itself was blocked (403/certificate mismatch), so treat as strongly likely rather than independently page-confirmed by this pass; non-EU fee reduced by a 30% tuition-fee waiver from the 2nd year of study

faculty: Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering; Faculty of Medicine
duration: 2 years, 120 ECTS; jointly organized by the Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering and the Faculty of Medicine (page-stated); three specialisation modules (names not detailed on the programme's own page); 50 study places annually; non-EU fee reduced by a 30% tuition-fee waiver from the 2nd year of study

faculty: Environmental and Chemical Engineering (Faculty of Technology)
duration: 2 years, 120 ECTS; four study options (Hydrology and Water Management, Industrial Environmental Engineering, Sustainable Energy Systems, Indoor Environmental Engineering); ~20 study places; 40% tuition-fee waiver available for 2nd year of study; next application period 7-21 Jan 2027 for autumn 2027 intake. Owning unit: the programme's own oulu.fi page names only 'Faculty of Technology,' no specific unit; attribution to Environmental and Chemical Engineering (ECE) is inferred via programme director Satu Pitkäaho's own University of Oulu staff profile, which lists her as a University Lecturer/Docent in ECE — a well-supported but not page-explicit attribution.

faculty: Industrial Engineering and Management (Faculty of Technology)
duration: 2 years, 120 ECTS; ASIIN and EUR-ACE accredited Industrial Engineering and Management degree programme; project-based curriculum run in collaboration with industry partners; 40% tuition-fee waiver available for 2nd year of study; next application period 7-21 Jan 2027 for autumn 2027 intake. Owning unit explicitly confirmed on Industrial Engineering and Management's own oulu.fi page, which states the unit offers this Master's programme.

course_name: Mining Engineering, Mineral Processing and Geophysics
faculty: Oulu Mining School (Faculty of Technology)
duration: 2 years, 120 ECTS; three study tracks (Mining Engineering, Mineral Processing, Geophysics); admission expects engineering or natural-science background (preferably geophysics, geosciences, physics or chemistry) plus completed coursework in Calculus, Differential Equations and Matrix Algebra; 40% tuition-fee waiver available for 2nd year of study; next application period 7-21 Jan 2027 for autumn 2027 intake. Owning unit explicitly stated on the programme's own oulu.fi page.

course_name: Chemistry of Sustainable Processes and Materials
faculty: Sustainable Chemistry (Faculty of Technology)
duration: 2 years, 120 ECTS; advanced studies across analytical, applied, inorganic, physical and/or organic chemistry, plus compulsory laboratory work and optional studies from other Faculty of Technology programmes; requires a Bachelor's degree in chemistry or a closely related field (e.g. Chemical Technology, Chemical Engineering); partly co-delivered with the Kokkola University Consortium Chydenius's Unit for Applied Chemistry per that consortium's own page; 40% tuition-fee waiver available for 2nd year of study; next application period 7-21 Jan 2027 for autumn 2027 intake. Owning unit: the programme's own oulu.fi page confirms only 'Faculty of Technology,' no specific unit; attribution to Sustainable Chemistry is inferred via programme director Matti Niemelä's own staff profile, which lists him as director of this degree programme and a lecturer in the Sustainable Chemistry research unit — a well-supported but not page-explicit attribution.

course_name: Geosciences, Mineral Resources and Sustainable Mining
faculty: Oulu Mining School (Faculty of Technology)
duration: 2 years, 120 ECTS; covers the technological, geological, financial, environmental and social aspects of sustainable mining across the whole mining value chain from exploration to mining, concentration, refining and closure; requires background of 60 ECTS in geology plus basic petrographic microscopy skills; fieldwork and lab work at the Oulu Mining School Research Center; 40% tuition-fee waiver available for 2nd year of study; next application period 7-21 Jan 2027 for autumn 2027 intake. Owning unit explicitly stated on the programme's own oulu.fi page.

faculty: Oulu School of Architecture (Faculty of Technology)
duration: 2 years, 120 ECTS; design-oriented programme at the northernmost architecture school in Europe; degree awarded is Master of Science (Architecture), a professional architect's qualification recognised in Finland and across the EU; 40% tuition-fee waiver available for 2nd year of study; next application period 7-21 Jan 2027 for autumn 2027 intake. Owning unit explicitly stated on the programme's own oulu.fi page.

course_name: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master's: Redesigning the Post-Industrial City (RePIC)
faculty: Oulu School of Architecture (Faculty of Technology)
duration: 2 years, 120 ECTS (4 semesters x 30 ECTS), an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM) delivered across 8 UNIC-alliance partner universities (University of Oulu, Ruhr-Universitat Bochum, Erasmus University Rotterdam, Koc University, University of Liege, University College Cork, University of Deusto, University of Zagreb); mandatory mobility, minimum one full semester at 2+ partner universities, common core curriculum in semester 1 at Ruhr-Universitat Bochum; AQAS-accredited. oulu.fi's own International Programmes page lists this only under 'Joint European Programmes' and links out to the consortium's own site (unic.eu/en/repic) rather than publishing a fee itself; that external page states ALL students, including EU/EEA/Swiss citizens, pay tuition (EUR 9,000 total for EU/EFTA, EUR 18,000 total for non-EU/EFTA, billed per semester) -- a genuine 'everyone pays' Erasmus Mundus exception -- but since oulu.fi itself never states this figure, both fee sides are recorded null per this project's sourcing rule rather than using the off-domain unic.eu figure. Owning unit inferred via programme director Prof. Helka-Liisa Hentila (Urban Design and Planning, Oulu School of Architecture)'s own University of Oulu staff profile, which names her as the RePIC/Faculty UNIC coordinator/director -- oulu.fi has no single dedicated programme page separate from its International Programmes listing and news coverage, so this is a director-profile inference rather than an explicit on-page 'delivered by' statement. Next application period 7-21 Jan 2027 for autumn 2027 intake, applications made via Ruhr University.
